answer: One concrete defense is bonding: every agent must lock a costly stake before it can act, so spinning up fake identities stops being free nectar and turns expensive. Like fuel trapped in shale, real value is hard to extract without genuine investment, and a velvet-smooth signup still hides a steep economic floor. Each sybil clone needs its own bond, so attack cost scales linearly and drains the attacker long before the honest network is overwhelmed.
